summary: Discovery focused on Mariners Financial's interest in Redwood Dedicated: reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and data isolation. Discussed burst-to-hosted, autoscaling policies, latency targets (P95), quantization and model variants, KMS/SSO requirements, and pilot approach. transcript:
Header: 2026-10-11 09:00 AM PDT | Duration: 56 minutes
Attendees: Tom Reynolds (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Alex Kim (Redwood CSM); Elena Park (Head of ML, Mariners), Marcus Lee (CTO), Ravi Shah (Infra Lead)

[00:00] Tom: Hey everyone, thanks for taking time. Tom from Redwood here, with Priya our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:05] Elena: Good, thanks. Busy, but excited to talk through dedicated options.
[00:12] Priya: Awesome. Quick agenda — understand current infra and constraints, workload profiles, latency and cost goals, security needs, and then how Redwood Dedicated would map to that with sizing and burst options.
[00:23] Marcus: Sounds good. I'll hand it over to Elena to give context on the ML workloads.
[00:28] Elena: Sure — we run a set of LLM features in prod: customer support summarization, document search + generation, and embeddings for semantic search. Most models today are hosted via vendor APIs but we're moving to dedicated infra for cost and data isolation. We're targeting 10k QPS for embeddings during peak and around 500 concurrent chat sessions. Latency expectations — P95 under 400ms for chat responses ideally, embeddings P95 under 150ms. We also need strict data residency and KMS integration.
[01:05] Priya: Got it. When you say vendor APIs today, is it a mix of OpenAI and other open models? Any on-prem attempts?
[01:12] Elena: Primarily OpenAI plus some experiments on Sagemaker and Replicate for self-hosted. But costs spiked and we lost control over routeability. So exploring Redwood Dedicated to have reserved GPU capacity with burst to hosted when needed.
[01:28] Tom: Perfect — that's exactly what Redwood Dedicated is designed for: reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput, and optional burst-to-hosted fallback. One quick Q: what's the percent of PII or regulated data flowing through?
[01:40] Marcus: About 35% of requests touch PII, customer identifying fields — so we need data isolation and audit logs, and integration with our KMS. SOC2 compliance is required.
[01:49] Alex: We can absolutely support KMS/HSM integrations, SSO, RBAC and audit logs. We have SOC2 and ISO materials we can share.
[01:56] Ravi: One operational thing — how does autoscaling work for dedicated? We need to absorb traffic bursts without blowing the commit.
[02:02] Priya: For Dedicated, you reserve a pool of GPUs for your tenant. You can configure autoscaling policies for the pool and set burst capacity that can spill over to Redwood hosted capacity. The routing policy supports cost-first or latency-first fallbacks.
[02:16] Ravi: So if we set a commit of, say, 10 A100 equiv nodes, and we hit 2x traffic, it'll either queue or burst to hosted?
[02:24] Priya: Correct. We can configure reserved burst credits that allow short-term bursts; beyond that we fallback to hosted endpoints with your policy. You can also set graceful degradation: route smaller models or quantized variants for non-critical requests.
[02:36] Elena: What's the granularity of model variants? We want to run 70B for higher-quality generation but fall back to 13B/8-bit quantized for cost-sensitive flows.
[02:46] Priya: We support model variants and quant profiles. For example you can pin a primary model and allow automatic fallback to a quantized variant or a smaller architecture. The runtime does KV cache management and continuous batching — that helps keep token costs down without sacrificing latency.
[02:58] Marcus: Ok — on latency, you said routing policy can prefer latency. Do you have SLO controls — like P95 under 400ms — how do we ensure that?
[03:07] Tom: We expose per-route SLOs and observability in the Redwood Console. For Dedicated we give token-level latency and cost breakdowns. You can set SLOs and get alerts when quality or latency regresses. For P95 targets we'll size the reserved pool based on your qps and request distribution; Priya can run a capacity plan.
[03:24] Priya: Right — we'll ask for a 72-hour sample trace or typical traffic shape, plus model sequence length distribution and payload sizes. From that we run a sizing sim and propose GPU counts and queueing characteristics.
[03:35] Ravi: We can share Prometheus metrics and a week of request logs, is that enough?
[03:39] Priya: Yes, that's perfect.
[03:41] Marcus: What's the billing model for committed capacity vs. burst?
[03:45] Tom: Reserved capacity is a monthly commit — predictable pricing based on GPU-equivalent units. Burst to hosted is billed at usage rates but you get configurable limits so it doesn't surprise you. We can show sample math in the pricing sheet.
[03:57] Elena: Security — we need SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, RBAC, audit trails, and KMS integration. Also data residency for EU requests.
[04:06] Alex: All supported. For Private deployments we offer VPC/on-prem options, but for Dedicated we support VPC peering and customer-managed networking plus KMS key wrapping. We'll attach the SOC2 and security docs after the call.
[04:18] Marcus: How about model onboarding? We run internally-tuned model checkpoints. Can we bring our custom weights?
[04:24] Priya: Yes, Dedicated supports customer models in a private registry. There are some kernel/compilation constraints depending on architecture and quantization. We'll vet it in onboarding and advise on quantization profiles.
[04:35] Ravi: Performance questions: we care about KV cache priming and multi-request batching. Does the runtime keep long-lived KV caches per session?
[04:42] Priya: The runtime supports KV caching and prefix caching. For chat sessions we keep session KV cache and can pin it to the node handling the session to avoid cache misses. That reduces tokens and latency. For throughput you can enable continuous batching which groups token generation across requests to increase GPU utilization with minimal latency impact.
[05:00] Elena: For the pilot, we want a 2-week dedicated cluster to run our top 3 models and compare cost/latency vs current vendor. Is that plausible?
[05:08] Tom: Totally plausible. We typically run a 2-week pilot with reserved trial capacity. We'll scope the trial size in the next deep dive.
[05:14] Marcus: On compliance, we may need a data processing addendum and contractual language about audit rights.
[05:20] Alex: We'll loop in legal and provide our standard DPA and SOC2 attestations. If needed we can escalate to customer success/enterprise sales for contractual tweaks.
[05:28] Tom: Quick competitor question — you mentioned Sagemaker and Replicate. Any other vendors you're evaluating?
[05:33] Elena: We're talking to Lambda Labs and a couple of managed inference providers, also evaluating long-term cost vs managed vendor APIs.
[05:40] Tom: Understood. Redwood differentiator here is the unified runtime and observability plus predictable economics for high-volume customers.
[05:47] Ravi: Small thing — what about maintenance windows and SLAs?
[05:51] Priya: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and maintenance windows typically scheduled with you; we have enterprise SLAs for latency and availability for reserved pools. We'll include that in the pricing/contract docs.
[06:02] Elena: Great.
[06:03] Tom: Alright let's recap and actions. We'll send pricing and commitment tiers, SOC2/security pack, and Priya will schedule the capacity planning deep dive. Mariners will share traffic samples, model list, and sample prompts. Pilot plan expected after the deep dive.
[06:18] Marcus: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[06:21] Elena: Thanks.
[06:23] (call ends)

Notes: rough transcription; some product names transcribed as "Redewood" or "Redwood Dedictaed" in places. Audio had a brief cut at ~00:03-00:05 causing a short gap. Shared artifacts referenced: pricing sheet (link to be sent), SOC2 pack (link), sample benchmark spreadsheet (to be shared).

Recap / Next steps (verbatim):
- Tom: I'll send pricing + commitment tiers and an example contract template.
- Priya: I'll schedule a technical deep dive to run capacity simulations and propose GPU counts.
- Mariners: share telemetry (QPS, payload sizes), model list, and top 10 prompts for benchmarking.
